newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh seeks help to build cyclone shelters.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh seeks help to build cyclone shelters.

text.p: Bangladesh on Thursday asked for international help for building more cyclone shelters in coastal areas to minimise casualty in future calamities.
"We have told international community that we need help for building 2,000 more shelters in cyclone prone areas," Foreign Secretary Farooq Sobhan told a news conference in Dhaka.

Sobhan said Foreign Minister Abdus Samad Azad, in a meeting with head of Dhaka-based foreign diplomatic missions and international aid agencies on Thursday, stressed on long-term requirements to face cyclone and other natural disasters.
"We also sought assistance for afforestation in coastal belt and raising of land in select areas."
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has already asked the authorities to take immediate steps for building an additional 2,000 shelters.
Sobhan said Bangladesh would not launch an international appeal for cyclone aid but accept help if friendly countries made offers.
"We won't launch any international appeal this time. We still think we have the means of our own to tackle the crisis," Sobhan quoted the Foreign Minister Azad as telling the foreign envoys.
Azad said that the country immediately needed house building materials, high protein biscuits and water purification plants.
"We briefed them about short and long term requirements as many were asking what (help) we might need," Sobhan said.
He said Dhaka's foreign office was constantly keeping Bangladesh missions abroad on the extent of damage in Monday's cyclone and asked them to brief local governments.
Sobhan said missions had been told to accept relief from expatriate Bangladeshis.
The official BSS news agency, quoting figures available from disaster control room in the prime minister's office, put the confirmed death toll by Thursday at 105.
But Hasina's office rejected press reports that hundreds of fishermen were still missing in the Bay of bengal since the cylone struck three days ago.
"We checked with relevent sources and we have not received any confirmation about those missing fishermen," press secretary to the prime minister, Jawadul Karim, told reporters.
Karim reconfirmed the official death toll was 105 on Thursday and said it might rise further with reports available from remote islands. REUTER SA AN
